top_entities.name: Valencia
top_entities.news_summary: Flash floods hit the Valencia area overnight 2026-09-16/17 (about 70 l/m2 in 30 minutes around Torrent), closing Valencia airport and Metrovalencia; the 22:08 ES-Alert was criticised by the DANA victims' association as too late, echoing the 2024 DANA failures. On 2026-09-21 former Generalitat president Carlos Mazon again appeared before the Congress inquiry commission and declined to disclose WhatsApp messages from the 2024 disaster, citing a High Court ruling.

top_entities.name: Egypt
top_entities.news_summary: CPJ and partners report that Egyptian security forces raided homes and arrested six investigative journalists (Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira, Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud, Mohamed Adel) between 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29 without publicly disclosing reasons; CPJ is demanding their release.

top_entities.name: Spain
top_entities.news_summary: The 2026-09-23 eviction of an 87-year-old woman (Maricarmen Abascal) set off nationwide housing protests: a protest encampment at Madrid's Puerta del Sol from 2026-09-26 and marches in 23 cities on 2026-09-28. The Sanchez government unveiled an urgent housing decree on 2026-09-29 (reported to include tenant protections and a temporary eviction ban where no alternative housing exists), and on 2026-09-30 the woman was reported returning home.

top_entities.name: Delta Air Lines
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-09-28 a federal court in Los Angeles tentatively approved (final approval order still expected) a $78.75M class settlement over the January 2020 Delta jet-fuel dump that doused schools and neighbourhoods in Cudahy/Bell, compensating roughly 38,000 property owners and residents; Delta denies wrongdoing and blames a mechanical issue. Reparative action for community harm.

top_entities.name: Pakistan
top_entities.news_summary: Ahead of a PTI-led march on Islamabad planned for 2026-09-27 demanding Imran Khan's release, authorities blocked roads around the capital with thousands of security personnel, closed Islamabad schools to house police, and detained Khan's sisters (Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan, Noreen Niazi) under Punjab's Maintenance of Public Order ordinance (reported 2026-09-24).

top_entities.name: Barrick Gold
top_entities.news_summary: Barrick Mining signed a new collective bargaining agreement with unions at its Loulo-Gounkoto gold mine in Mali on 2026-09-28 (agreement reached 2026-09-21), averting a planned strike; positive labour outcome at a site previously subject to a state dispute.

top_entities.name: Cornell University
top_entities.news_summary: Cornell issued a statement on 2026-09-21 about a lawsuit alleging that a student was sexually assaulted by seven students at a fraternity house in 2024 and that the university failed to protect her and improperly sanctioned the respondents; reporting says the New York Attorney General announced a review of Cornell's initial response, and the Boston Globe (2026-09-30) reports the case reopened amid campus anger and debate about sexual assault.

top_entities.name: Kingston
top_entities.news_summary: Police fatally shot alleged gang leader Amani Malcolm in Denham Town, Kingston on 2026-09-18; residents protested overnight and on 2026-09-19, burning a vehicle, and a man was reportedly set on fire after refusing to join the protest; the matter was reported to the Independent Commission of Investigations (INDECOM).

top_entities.name: Tennessee
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-09-30 Tennessee's execution of Christa Pike failed: she survived the lethal injection protocol (reported as two doses of pentobarbital), was hospitalised, and Governor Bill Lee halted the execution and then all state executions pending an independent review; the 6th Circuit had briefly blocked the execution before the US Supreme Court allowed it to proceed. Health workers say the method flouts medical ethics; this follows a botched execution in May 2026.

top_entities.name: Somalia
top_entities.news_summary: UN humanitarian coordinator for Somalia George Conway issued a statement on 2026-09-28 warning that fighting in Baidoa is driving repeated displacement and worsening child malnutrition; an IPC analysis released around 2026-09-23 projects about 26,000 displaced people in Baidoa at risk of famine by year-end (Baidoa hosts more than half a million displaced people).

top_entities.name: Myanmar
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-09-28 a Myanmar military airstrike hit a crowded market and adjacent bridge in a town in the Arakan Army-held west, killing 33 and wounding 36 per the Arakan Army (toll later reported at 50); separately, Malaysia began returning about 1,500 Myanmar nationals on 2026-09-29. This is a new 2026 event distinct from the school strike dated 2025-09-12 already held in the misdated-claims ledger.

top_entities.name: University of Glasgow
top_entities.news_summary: A Liberty Investigates/Al Jazeera investigation published 2026-09-24 reports that UK universities, including Glasgow and Birmingham, discussed campus pro-Palestine protests with arms maker BAE Systems, which funds them with up to GBP 15M a year under long-term agreements.

top_entities.name: University of Birmingham
top_entities.news_summary: A Liberty Investigates/Al Jazeera investigation published 2026-09-24 reports that UK universities, including Birmingham and Glasgow, discussed campus pro-Palestine protests with arms maker BAE Systems, which funds them with up to GBP 15M a year under long-term agreements.

top_entities.name: OpenAI
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-09-28 Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier e-filed (Highlands County Circuit Court) a motion for a temporary injunction against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman seeking to pause new model development absent independent safety guardrails and to bar minors in Florida from using ChatGPT; a federal judge had earlier remanded the case to state court.

top_entities.name: Laos
top_entities.news_summary: RFA (2026-09-25) reports a Lao content creator who disappeared in Thailand (noticed 2026-09-16, reported to police 2026-09-18) may be a case of transnational repression, per an NGO.

top_entities.name: Vietnam
top_entities.news_summary: A rights group alleges Vietnamese authorities abducted an Australian man (Hiep Tran) and a Norwegian-Vietnamese colleague in Cambodia and forcibly took them to Vietnam (ABC, 2026-09-29); allegation, not independently confirmed.

top_entities.name: United States
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-09-29 the US Supreme Court paused a lower-court order and allowed the administration to resume rapid third-country deportations without prior notice while it takes up the case for argument in December; plaintiffs allege deportees (more than 25,000 sent to 29 countries per reports) were detained indefinitely, abused, or sent on to places where they fear torture.

top_entities.name: Northwestern University
top_entities.news_summary: The Daily Northwestern (2026-09-29) reports that an ACLU/Amnesty International USA report (released 2026-09-23, covering 80 campuses) cites Northwestern for punitive discipline and restrictions on pro-Palestinian speech and protest.

top_entities.name: Meta Platforms
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-09-25 a Santa Fe, New Mexico jury found Meta liable under the state's Unfair Practices Act in a second trial, finding Facebook deceived users about privacy protections; this follows the 2026-03-24 verdict in the same state's child-safety case (reported $375M penalties). Remedies/penalties phase pending.

top_entities.name: Madrid
top_entities.news_summary: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid on 2026-09-26/27 over Spain's housing crisis and the eviction of an 87-year-old woman; protesters camped in the Puerta del Sol plaza outside the regional government headquarters, with 600+ residents in the camp by 2026-09-28.

top_entities.name: New York City
top_entities.news_summary: More than 100 people were arrested on 2026-09-24 as New Yorkers protested Israeli PM Netanyahu's UN visit, including a Jewish Voice for Peace sit-in blocking a road outside UN headquarters (Al Jazeera, 2026-09-25).

top_entities.name: South Africa
top_entities.news_summary: Al Jazeera (2026-09-28) reports refugees and migrants in South Africa fear new xenophobic attacks as an anti-migrant 'deadline' of 2026-09-30 looms, with police standing between rival groups at tense protests and concerns about police accountability.

top_entities.name: Cambodia
top_entities.news_summary: A rights group alleges Vietnamese authorities abducted an Australian man (Hiep Tran) and a Norwegian-Vietnamese colleague on Cambodian soil and forcibly took them to Vietnam (ABC, 2026-09-29); allegation, not independently confirmed.

top_entities.name: Bangladesh
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch (2026-09-22) reports that three laws approved by Bangladesh's parliament in September reverse human-rights protections created under the 2024-2026 interim government, weakening safeguards against enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings and breaking the ruling BNP's reform commitments.

top_entities.name: Turkey
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch (2026-09-18) and Amnesty report a coordinated crackdown on LGBT rights groups: police raids on seven groups on 2026-09-12 to 14, at least 112 (HRW) to 116 (Amnesty) people arrested across 15 provinces, at least 82-83 held in pretrial detention, and criminal investigations against more than 160 people.

top_entities.name: Iran
top_entities.news_summary: The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran presented its report to the Human Rights Council on 2026-09-21 finding crimes against humanity in the January 2026 suppression of nationwide protests (mass killings, detention, torture, a nearly five-month internet shutdown, intensified death penalty use); CPJ reports Iran sentenced journalist Abbas Abdi to a year in prison and ordered the newspaper Etemad suspended on 2026-09-27.

top_entities.name: Hong Kong
top_entities.news_summary: Hong Kong police arrested Tang Ho-wing, founder of the online outlet Boom News, on the morning of 2026-09-30 on suspicion of incitement/sedition over alleged disinformation (Al Jazeera, 2026-09-30).

sector_alerts.title: AI governance wave: state and federal actions against frontier labs
sector_alerts.summary: Florida AG sought a temporary injunction against OpenAI (2026-09-28); California signed SB 947 limiting automated firing and discipline (2026-09-30) after children's-chatbot rules on 2026-09-10; Rep. Ro Khanna announced an AI safety bill with a ban on 'recursive' self-improvement until safeguards exist (2026-09-28); a class action filed 2026-09-18 alleges Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI coordinated an AI slowdown. Entity-level evidence recorded for OpenAI; other labs touched at sector level only.

sector_alerts.title: Campus speech and sexual-violence scrutiny: US universities
sector_alerts.summary: ACLU/Amnesty USA report (2026-09-23, 80 campuses) on suppression of pro-Palestinian speech; US Commission on Civil Rights antisemitism enforcement report transmitted 2026-09-28; Cornell sexual-assault lawsuit and NY AG review (entity-level evidence recorded).

sector_alerts.title: Press-freedom crackdowns: Iran, Egypt, Hong Kong
sector_alerts.summary: CPJ documented Iran's sentencing of journalist Abbas Abdi (2026-09-27), the arrest of six Egyptian investigative journalists (2026-09-28/29) and Hong Kong's arrest of Boom News founder Tang Ho-wing (2026-09-30). Entity-level evidence recorded for each.

sector_alerts.title: Housing-rights protests across Spain
sector_alerts.summary: Protests in 23 Spanish cities on 2026-09-28 after the 2026-09-23 eviction of an 87-year-old; encampments in Madrid and reportedly Seville and other cities; government decree 2026-09-29. Entity-level evidence recorded for Spain and Madrid; Seville/Barcelona/Valencia city mentions are secondary (Seville's rests on an undated Wikipedia page and is not used).

sector_alerts.title: Corporate DEI retreat and layoff trend (sector context)
sector_alerts.summary: Forbes (2026-09-24) reports companies that dropped DEI have little to show; Fortune 500 participation in the HRC Corporate Equality Index fell from 377 (2025) to 131 (2026) per a Fox Business-reported study; Molson Coors told employees in early September it is dropping representation goals. Sector mention only; no entity-specific in-window event verified.

sector_alerts.title: Disaster cluster: Japan typhoon, South/Southeast Asia floods, Hurricane Polo
sector_alerts.summary: Typhoon Dujuan (2026-09-21) put more than 1.9 million people under evacuation orders in Japan; floods and landslides killed 56 in India, 14 in Nepal and 8 in Thailand (2026-09-25..27); Vietnam flooding affected 16,000+ homes (2026-09-18); Hurricane Polo struck Baja California Sur (2026-09-24). Context for city/country response assessments; no entity-level conduct finding.

sector_alerts.title: Displacement and famine risk: UNHCR Security Council briefing and Somalia
sector_alerts.summary: UNHCR told the Security Council 117 million people are forcibly displaced and funding cuts threaten assistance to 8.3 million (2026-09-25); Somalia/Baidoa famine-risk warnings (entity-level evidence recorded).

sector_alerts.title: Context only (outside window): Abbott infant-formula settlement
sector_alerts.summary: Abbott agreed to pay $385M to resolve DOJ/state claims over the 2022 Sturgis infant-formula plant contamination, announced 2026-09-14 (statnews.com/2026/09/14; Abbott press release 2026-09-14). This is 3 days before the 2026-09-17 window start and therefore does not drive an assess flag; noted for the assessor as context.
